A thrill-seeker is flying through the air with a surfboard attached to his feet, showing off a new extreme sport. This photo was taken in Estavayer-le-Lac, Switzerland, where a new water sport called "Jet Surfing" has become very popular. The device jumps high above the water, looking like the futuristic hoverboard from the movie *Back to the Future*, where the character Marty McFly rides a flying board. See the video below. Jet surfing is the newest trend in extreme water sports, as brave riders push it to new heights.

Ashley Young wants to stop Manchester United from losing five games in a row against their local rivals, Manchester City. Even though United has won more trophies in the past, City has been beating them more often in recent years. City won their fourth game in a row last November with a 1-0 score at the Etihad Stadium. The last time City won four games in a row against United was 60 years ago.

United has now lost the last four derbies to City. The most recent loss was on April 8, 2013, when City won 2-1. However, Ander Herrera scored a goal for United, which helped them move above City in the standings for the first time this season.

Adian Rodley, a New Zealand racing agent, became famous online after a video showed his excited reaction to a horse winning a big race.

The horse, Mongolian Khan, ridden by jockey Opie Bosson, won the Australian Derby. This important race took place on Monday at Randwick and had a prize of $2 million.

Rodley was watching the race on Trackside TV. He did not know he was being filmed when he started celebrating. As the horse got closer to the finish line, Rodley became happier and happier. The funny video of his celebration has now gone viral.

A group of wild wood bison was successfully released in Alaska, marking the first time in more than 100 years that they have roamed freely on the plains. Video shows Alaska Department of Fish and Game Biologist Tom Seaton leading 100 bison to their new home on a snowmobile. The animals were let out of a temporary pen, where they had stayed for just over a week during the move, and followed Mr. Seaton. They traveled about a mile, crossed the Innoko River, and arrived at the grassy meadows of Lower Innoko, which is near the Yukon River.

Novak Djokovic beat David Ferrer 7-5, 7-5 to reach the semi-finals of the Miami Open. This means he will likely play Andy Murray next. Murray is also in the semi-finals, where he will face Tomas Berdych.

Ferrer started the match strongly, winning the first three games and playing better than the world number one, Djokovic. However, he could not keep up that speed. Djokovic eventually caught up and won the match. This victory came on Ferrer’s 33rd birthday.

Tryster, the favorite, won the Coral Easter Classic at Lingfield by three-quarters of a length. His win helped his trainer, Charlie Appleby, and his team, Godolphin, dominate the £1.1 million All Weather Finals day.

Tryster is a four-year-old horse ridden by jockey William Buick. He beat another horse named Complicit. This victory completed a "treble" (three wins) for trainer Charlie Appleby, with odds of 22-1. Appleby had already won two other races that day:
*   The Unibet Sprint Championship Stakes, won by Pretend (also ridden by Buick).
*   The 32Red Three-Year-old Mile Championship, won by Four Seasons (ridden by Adam Kirby

There are likely eight Irish horses running in next week’s £1 million Crabbie’s Grand National. Trainer Robbie Hennessy has confirmed that Rubi Light will definitely run.

Rubi Light won a major race over two and a half miles on Saturday. He practiced jumping over fences like those at Aintree with jockey Andrew Lynch.

Although Rubi Light could have run in the shorter Topham Chase on Friday, Hennessy said he is going to run in the Grand National instead. Hennessy explained, “There is only one National.”

He also noted that Rubi Light once finished second in a three-mile race (the Lexus Chase) behind a horse named Synchronised. That same season, Rubi Light went on to win the Gold Cup.

Trainer Paul Webber hopes the ground at Fairyhouse dries out more before Sunday’s race. He is preparing Cantlow, a horse, to help AP McCoy have a great final race in Ireland. If Cantlow wins the Irish Grand National on Easter Monday, it would be McCoy’s second victory in this race.

McCoy won the 2007 race on a horse named Butler’s Cabin. Winning again on Cantlow would be a perfect start to what might be McCoy’s last week as a jockey. He has promised to retire right away if he wins Saturday’s Crabbie’s Grand National at Aintree on his favorite horse, Shutthefrontdoor. Shutthefrontdoor is a gelding that won last year’s Irish National under jockey Barry Gerag

Mark McCall thinks that playing in neutral locations gives Saracens a good chance of beating the strong Clermont team to reach their second European final in a row.

On Sunday, Marcelo Bosch kicked a long-distance penalty at the very end of the match against Racing Metro. This scored point gave Saracens a 12-11 win and secured their spot in the semi-finals. They will now travel to St Etienne’s Stade Geoffroy-Guichard on April 18.

Their opponent in the semi-finals is Clermont. Clermont is feeling very confident after they easily defeated Northampton, who were leading the Aviva Premiership, with a score of 37-5.

Munster has signed New Zealand player Francis Saili for two years. He is a versatile back who played his first game for the All Blacks against Argentina in 2013. He will join Munster later this year after finishing his current contract in 2015. The 24-year-old currently plays for the Blues, a Super Rugby team based in Auckland. He also helped New Zealand’s Under-20 team win the Junior World Championship in Italy in 2011. Munster head coach Anthony Foley thinks Saili is a great addition to their team and considers the signing a major success.

Anthony Watson, who plays for England and Bath, thinks that the disappointment of losing in the European Champions Cup can help motivate his team to reach the Aviva Premiership play-offs this season.

Bath lost to Leinster 18-15 in Dublin. Leinster won because their player, Ian Madigan, kicked six successful penalties. It was a close match.

Bath played very well for much of the second half. They scored two tries, one by George Ford and one by team captain Stuart Hooper. However, Bath made too many mistakes, which caused them to lose. This loss means they will not reach the semi-finals, which they last did in 2006.

Tiger Woods says the Par-3 Contest is about having fun and enjoying the game, not about winning. He played in the tournament for the first time since 2004. He made it a family event by bringing his girlfriend, Lindsey Vonn, and having his children help him carry his golf clubs. When asked about his goals, Woods said he just wants to have fun and not win, no matter what happens. He was playing six strokes under par after eight holes, but then he accidentally hit two balls into the water on the ninth hole.

Jack Grealish has told Premier League referees that he will not change how he wears his socks, no matter what they say. The Aston Villa player is known for wearing his socks low, just above his shinpads. He plans to keep doing this after making his first Premier League start on Tuesday night. Grealish, who plays for the Ireland Under-21 team, wears children’s shinpads and says he will not change his habit. He explained to the BBC that wearing his socks this way is a superstition he has followed his whole life.

Tim Bresnan believes that starting the domestic season well with Yorkshire, the current County Championship champions, could help him get called back to the England Test team. He last played for England’s second team during the 5-0 Ashes loss in the winter of 2013/14. However, he has recently trained with the main England squad before the World Cup in Australia and played for the England Lions during their tour of South Africa.

More importantly, Bresnan helped Yorkshire end a 13-year wait for a title last season. He took 30 wickets in 10 games, with an average of 31.57, and scored 95 runs against Nottinghamshire on the day the championship was won.

Stuart Broad recovered from an injury scare, and Jonny Bairstow scored 98, just missing a century, as England’s practice match against the West Indies felt more like a training session than a real game.

The match at Lord’s, where officials decided to remove Paul Downton as managing director of the England and Wales Cricket Board, seemed more important for the future of English cricket. In contrast, the game at Warner Park was a mixed-up event where four English players were added to the local team.

Jonathan Trott scored 0 and Gary Ballance scored 17, so they did not help much. However, Bairstow made 98, and Joe Root finished the day with 87 not out. The local team reached 303

Even though Everton is currently in the lower half of the Premier League, nearly 4,000 loyal fans came to watch an open training session at Goodison Park on Tuesday. The club held this event during the school half-term break to prepare for their upcoming match against Swansea City, which takes place on Saturday at the Liberty Stadium. Fans were invited to watch manager Roberto Martinez train the players for free. Additionally, players John Stones and Aaron Lennon stayed behind to meet and greet fans at the club’s megastore.

Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parish wants to bring in more money to improve the club’s stadium, Selhurst Park. The team recently beat Manchester City 2-1. Reports say American businessman Josh Harris, who owns the Philadelphia 76ers and New Jersey Devils, wants to buy the club. However, Parish, who helped save the club from financial trouble in 2010, says he wants to stay involved. He prefers adding investment rather than selling the club completely.

Jack Grealish wants to turn his bad memories of Wembley Stadium into happy ones when Aston Villa plays Liverpool in the FA Cup semi-final. As a fan, the 19-year-old visited the stadium twice as a teenager to support his favorite team, but they lost both times: once to Manchester United in the League Cup final and once to Chelsea in the FA Cup final.

Grealish recently got his first start in the Premier League, playing in a 3-3 tie with Queens Park Rangers. This start was given to him by coach Tim Sherwood. Now, he hopes to keep his spot in the team for the match on April 19.

Julian Speroni has signed a new one-year contract with Crystal Palace, meaning he will play for the club for his 12th season. The goalkeeper originally joined the team from Dundee in July 2004. This new deal will last until the end of next season.

Speroni, who is 35 years old, has been a key player for Palace this season as they try to stay in the Barclays Premier League. He recently made a diving save against Yaya Toure on Monday night. At the end of the season, Speroni will play in a testimonial match against his former team, Dundee.

Andy King scored a winning goal in the 86th minute. The match wasn’t very pretty, but the victory kept Leicester City’s chance of staying in the Premier League alive for now.

The end of the game was very intense. Leicester manager Nigel Pearson and his players knew they had to win against West Ham. If they didn’t get three points, they would be relegated. West Ham had not won an away game since December 2nd.

When the game ended, the players went to all four corners of the stadium to thank their fans. Leicester is now only four points behind Sunderland. They have six of their last eight games at home. The fight to stay in the league is still very much on.

Paul McShane told his Hull teammates that they need to realize they are fighting to avoid being relegated. It would have been better if someone had said this before they arrived in Swansea on Saturday. If Hull is relegated, which seems likely based on their remaining games, this match will be one of the biggest mistakes they regret. It was strange to see Steve Bruce’s players so slow and uninterested in the first half, especially since the opposing team had nothing to gain from the game. Paul McShane scored for Hull, but they still lost 3-1 to Swansea at the Liberty Stadium.

Haris Vuckic says he doesn’t know where he will play next season, but he thinks Rangers would be a good choice if Newcastle allows him to leave. He is a young player from Newcastle who was sent to Rangers on loan on the last day of the January transfer window. He was one of five players sent to Glasgow. Because other players like Kevin Mbabu, Remie Streete, Gael Bigirimana, and Shane Ferguson were injured, 22-year-old Vuckic is the only one who has done well at Rangers. He is also a player for the Slovenia national team. He has only one year left on his contract with Newcastle, so he is not sure about his future.

James Ward-Prowse has spent his career staying out of the spotlight, so the quiet scene outside the Riverside Stadium on Monday night was fitting. He had just led England’s Under-21 team to a close 3-2 win against Germany by scoring the winning goal after a great 34-pass play. Usually, this kind of success would mean fans crowd around him to celebrate as he heads to the team bus. But this time, it was very calm. Ward-Prowse smiled and said, “I like signing autographs and giving back to fans, but there was no one there! It was empty! It was wet and windy, so everyone went home.”

Tony Pulis agrees that Joey Barton was likely right when he said West Bromwich Albion’s players were scared during their loss to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. In December, West Brom was winning 2-0 but lost to a hat-trick by Charlie Austin. This loss led to Barton’s harsh criticism and nearly got manager Alan Irvine fired. At the time, Barton said, “West Brom went 2-0 up and I turned to Dunney (Richard Dunne) and said, ‘they’ve scored too early.’ They don’t know how to finish the game.” Pulis has now admitted that Barton probably had a point about West Brom losing their composure.

Radamel Falcao, a striker for Manchester United, says that Sergio Aguero, who plays for Manchester City, is his team’s biggest threat. Falcao and Aguero were at an event for Puma shoes called #HeadtoHead. At the event, Falcao praised the upcoming Manchester derby. He said that Manchester City is a very talented team with dangerous players all over the field. However, he noted that Aguero has been especially dangerous for United in past games. Since joining City in 2011, Aguero has scored six goals against United.

It is that time of year when English teams in Europe struggle against teams with more money and face difficult rules about how much they can spend on players. This year, Dai Young, the director of rugby for Wasps, warned about these problems.

Wasps played very well in their Champions Cup quarter-final match against Toulon on Sunday, but they lost. The game showed how strong Toulon was. They brought in two of the world’s best players, Matt Giteau and Juan Fernandez Lobbe, as substitutes. They also had other top players, like Bryan Habana and Juan Smith, who did not play in the match.

Tottenham Hotspur is moving forward with building a new stadium at White Hart Lane. The first step is demolishing Archway Sheet Metal Works, a business located next to the stadium site.

The club plans to open the new 56,000-seat stadium in just over three years. They have received the necessary planning permission and won a legal battle against a compulsory purchase order.

Archway Sheet Metal Works had fought a long court case to stop the development. However, after losing an appeal earlier this year, their building is now being torn down.

Reece Oxford, a 16-year-old player for West Ham, got closer to making his first appearance for the main team by scoring a goal for the Under-21s. He scored with a header in a 3-2 loss to Manchester United on Tuesday night. Oxford has been on the bench for the senior team this season, and this goal strengthens his case for making his senior debut before the season ends.

After Celtic beat St Mirren 2-0 on Friday, Celtic manager Ronny Deila said that most pitches in the Scottish Premiership are "terrible" and suggested that artificial turf would make for better games.

Gary Teale, who works for St Mirren, disagreed with Deila. He said the criticism was unfair to St Mirren’s head groundsman, Tommy Docherty, who has won awards for his work. Teale stated that he was surprised by Deila’s comments because he believes St Mirren’s pitch is the best in the league.

Josh Harrop scored a key goal as Manchester United’s Under 21 team beat West Ham United to move four points ahead at the top of the league.

West Ham, who are at the bottom of the table, took a surprise lead early in the game. Just ten minutes in, Reece Oxford headed in a good pass from Josh Cullen. This was Oxford’s first away goal since September, but their lead only lasted 12 minutes. Harrop scored to tie the game, and then Joe Rothwell scored a few minutes later to complete the comeback.

Adnan Januzaj, who was the captain for Manchester United, led the team to this important win.

Ronny Deila agrees with Gary Teale that St Mirren has one of the best pitches in the Scottish Premiership. However, Deila thinks this is a criticism of other teams, not a compliment to St Mirren. After his team won 2-0 on Friday night, Deila criticized the playing surface at St Mirren Park. He said that most of the stadiums his team visits would be better if they had artificial pitches.

Gary Teale, the manager of St Mirren, disagreed. He said the pitch might be a little hard, but it is still excellent. He pointed out that their groundskeeper, Tommy, wins "pitch of the year" every year. Teale said this is a great honor for Tommy.

After Cristiano Ronaldo scored five goals in Real Madrid’s 9-1 win over Granada, his teammate Karim Benzema called him a “phenomenon.” This was the first time in Ronaldo’s career that he scored five goals in one game. It also made him only the third player to reach 300 goals for Madrid, which he did in just 287 games. On Sunday, Benzema said on the club’s website, “Cristiano is a phenomenon. He is always looking for goals and ways to help the team. He deserves everything he has achieved.”

Stuart McCall says his future at Rangers will not be decided before the season ends. He says his work to improve the team has not yet achieved enough. Since taking over last month, he has won the fans' support with three straight wins, including victories over Hibs and Hearts. He is now preparing for tonight's game against Queen of the South. McCall, who used to manage Motherwell, signed a contract until the end of the season to help the team try to get promoted.

Louis van Gaal is known for being a strict manager, but he showed a different side when he talked about Ander Herrera’s first goal for Manchester United against Aston Villa. Van Gaal said he was very happy with the goal. Before the game, he had asked Herrera to control the ball better before shooting, so he could show more calmness. When the players came back from halftime leading 1-0 because of Herrera’s goal in the 43rd minute, Van Gaal got so excited that he lost his cool.

England traveled to the Caribbean on Thursday with a clear goal: they must defeat the West Indies in their first Test match since returning to the format. This win is crucial for saving the jobs of key team members and stopping rumors about Kevin Pietersen. The pressure is high because England recently had a terrible World Cup, and Colin Graves, the new head of the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), has made it clear that players and staff could lose their positions. The three-match series starts in Antigua on April 13.

If Christian Benteke does not score enough goals to help Aston Villa stay in the Premier League, he will have to accept a significant pay cut. However, if he keeps scoring, other clubs will likely be interested in signing him.

Regardless of whether Aston Villa stays in the league or not, Benteke’s future will be a topic of discussion. His current contract pays him £50,000 a week and has two years left. The Belgian striker wants to play in European competitions.

Wolfsburg has been watching Benteke for over a year, even before he tore his Achilles tendon 12 months ago. They are still looking for a striker and have kept Benteke in mind.

Arsenal is interested in signing 21-year-old Argentine forward Paolo Dybala, who says he might be playing his last games for Palermo. Palermo’s president, Maurizio Zamparini, says that both Arsenal and Juventus have made offers for the player. Dybala has played very well in Serie A this season, scoring 13 league goals, which has attracted interest from many top European clubs. Although Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has denied that they want to sign him, Dybala is valued at £30 million and is likely to move to a new club this summer.

Amir Khan, a boxer from Bolton, spent his Friday at a safari park in northern California with his family. He visited Six Flags Discovery Kingdom with his wife, Faryal Makhdoom Khan, and their daughter, Lamysa. During the trip, the 28-year-old boxer posed with and fed a rare but dangerous white tiger. He also took photos with giraffes and sea lions while enjoying some time off with his family.

James Rodriguez is back with Real Madrid. The Spanish newspaper Marca reports that coach Carlo Ancelotti now has players from six different countries available. Rodriguez had been injured since early February, but he is starting the game against Granada on Sunday. This gives Ancelotti a strong attacking team with players from many nations to help compete with Barcelona in the final league matches. The starting lineup includes Toni Kroos (Germany), Karim Benzema (France), and Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal) in the back, and Gareth Bale (Wales), James Rodriguez (Colombia), and Luka Modric (Croatia) in the front.

Chelsea is talking about going on a tour after the season ends. This plan might cause problems for many international team managers. Jose Mourinho said it is possible for the team to travel 12,000 miles round-trip to Japan, where their new sponsors, Yokohama Rubber, are based. They have not chosen a final destination yet. If the tour happens, the team will likely leave on May 28 or 29 for a week-long trip that includes two matches. This news might worry many international coaches, who need Chelsea players for their friendlies and qualifiers in mid-June.

Blackburn Rovers manager Gary Bowyer is angry about FA Cup rules that stop him from playing a specific player against Liverpool in Wednesday’s replay at Ewood Park. The rule prevents him from using John O'Sullivan because O'Sullivan was on loan when the first match took place on March 9.

Bowyer really wanted to play 21-year-old midfielder John O'Sullivan, who has recently returned to Blackburn from a loan at Barnsley. This is especially important because Bowyer has many injured players at his Championship club. However, the FA did not make an exception. The reason is that O'Sullivan was playing for Barnsley at the time of the initial 0-0 draw at Anfield.

Burnley manager Sean Dyche is sure his team will avoid being relegated. The team is getting ready for their last eight games in the Barclays Premier League. They feel refreshed after a training trip to Spain in warm weather. The squad, which was missing four players who were playing for their national teams, spent last week in Spain. They are preparing for a final stretch of games that starts with a difficult match against Tottenham on Sunday. Sean Dyche believes his team can stay in the Premier League.

Napoli’s president, Aurelio De Laurentiis, has warned that he will send his players to a training camp for as long as necessary if they do not start playing better before the season ends. He was angry after his team lost 1-0 to Lazio at home on Wednesday. This loss meant Napoli lost the Coppa Italia semi-final 2-1 overall. This defeat added to a streak of five Serie A games without a win. Because of this, Napoli has dropped from third place to sixth place, making it very unlikely they will qualify for next season’s Champions League.

LeBron James hurt Miami’s chances of making the playoffs by scoring 23 points in the Cleveland Cavaliers’ 114-88 victory over the Heat on Thursday. James, who won two NBA championships with Miami before returning to Ohio, helped his team win at the American Airlines Arena. Kyrie Irving also scored 23 points for Cleveland. Meanwhile, Miami’s Dwyane Wade suffered a knee injury in the first half. Luol Deng added 17 points for Miami, but the team is worried about their standing in the Eastern Conference. They are in ninth place, tied with Boston, and need to watch their backs. LeBron James and Kyrie Irving both scored 23 points as the Cavaliers won in Miami.

Blackpool drew 1-1 with Reading, a result that confirmed their relegation to Sky Bet League One. However, the anger from fans was focused on the club’s chairman, Karl Oyston, rather than the game itself.

Blackpool’s drop to the third tier was officially confirmed on Easter Monday. This news led to protests by supporters outside the stadium (Bloomfield Road) before the match on Tuesday. Dozens of fans gathered near the West Stand 45 minutes before kickoff. They threw eggs at the back of the directors' boxes and tossed flares, smoke bombs, and fireworks into a restricted area in front of the main reception. These protests were a response to how the Oyston family has managed the club.

On the second morning of England’s first tour match in the West Indies, England captain Alastair Cook scored 101 runs. He had started the day with 95 runs. He reached 100 easily, hitting his 11th boundary on the first ball of the day and scoring two more runs in the next over. After reaching 101 off 200 balls, he shook hands with his partner, Gary Ballance, and left the field.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers says his team must play well in their next big game if they want to finish in the top four. Before the international break, Liverpool’s 13-game unbeaten streak ended with a home loss to Manchester United, a team fighting for Champions League spots. This loss left Liverpool five points behind the places that qualify for European competitions. Losing to third-place Arsenal would be a major setback for Liverpool’s goal of returning to top-level European competition for two years in a row. Rodgers has urged his players to do well in Saturday’s match against Arsenal.

This match was very different from the intense pressure of the Ashes series. It was a calm day of scoring runs against a weaker team in the beautiful city of Basseterre, during the start of England’s tour of the Caribbean. This quiet success meant a lot to Jonathan Trott.

Almost 18 months ago, during England’s difficult Ashes tour in Australia, Trott was heavily criticized by bowler Mitchell Johnson. After that, he felt he might never play for England again. He had to leave the team because of mental health issues.

Now, Trott has recovered. He has been chosen to open the batting in the first Test match in Antigua next week. This is a major comeback for him.

Jacques Burger represents everything rugby marketers like to talk about: loyalty, bravery, strength, and dedication. At Saracens, who play Racing Metro in Paris this Sunday for a spot in the European Champions Cup quarter-finals, his teammates love him just as much as his opponents hate him. Opponents fear how recklessly and fiercely he plays. After years of getting hit hard, his face is scarred and bruised, but he is exactly the kind of player you want on your team. Burger says, “I become a different person when I play rugby. My personality changes. When I leave the field, I become someone else again. It’s strange.”

Jose Mourinho says he doesn’t care where Chelsea wins the Premier League title, as long as they win it. Chelsea is currently six points ahead in the standings and has one game left to play. They play Stoke City at home this Saturday, which is the first of their last nine games of the season.

“I don’t care if we win in a hotel, away, or at home. I just want to win,” Mourinho said during training at Chelsea’s facility on Friday. He spoke at a press conference before the match against Stoke. Eden Hazard will start for Chelsea against Stoke on Saturday after a tiring break for international games.

Saturday’s game against Arsenal is very important for Liverpool’s hopes of reaching the Champions League. In December, Liverpool drew 2-2 with Arsenal. That game helped Liverpool become one of the best teams in the Premier League. After that, they went 13 games without losing. This put them in a good position to qualify for Europe’s top soccer competition. However, they lost to Manchester United in a dramatic match two weeks ago. Juan Mata scored a difficult goal in that game. Because of the loss, Liverpool is now five points behind Manchester United, who are in fourth place. Brendan Rodgers’ team must beat Arsenal on Saturday to keep their chance of finishing in the top four.

Olivier Giroud won the Barclays Premier League Player of the Month award for March. This makes him the most successful foreign player in the league’s history. He is now the 16th French player to win this honor.

Giroud scored five goals during Arsenal’s four straight league wins last month. His team earned all 12 possible points, which helped him win the award. By winning, he joins many other famous French players, such as Thierry Henry, Eric Cantona, and Nicolas Anelka, who have also been named the best player in a month.

Liverpool plays Arsenal on Saturday in the early Premier League match. Based on past games, we might see a lot of goals. Since the Premier League started, five hat-tricks have been scored in matches between these two teams. This is one more than in matches between Newcastle United and Manchester United.

In December, the teams played at Anfield and tied 2-2. Martin Skrtel scored the equalizing goal in the final moments of the game. Also, in 1994, Robbie Fowler scored the fastest hat-trick in Premier League history while playing for Liverpool against Arsenal.

Liverpool players Mario Balotelli, Fabio Borini, Rickie Lambert, and Lazar Markovic were surprised when YouTube star Bas van Velzen visited their training ground, Melwood. The players thought he was just a regular fan who had won a contest to meet them and learn how to take free kicks. However, after a few practice shots, it became clear that Van Velzen was very skilled at scoring goals. The photo shows (from left to right) Rickie Lambert, Fabio Borini, Lazar Markovic, and Mario Balotelli meeting Bas van Velzen.

Kenwyne Jones came off the bench late in the game and scored just three minutes after his first appearance for Bournemouth. This goal helped Bournemouth tie the match against Ipswich, even though they had gone behind early to a goal by Freddie Sears.

Bournemouth controlled most of the game but had to wait until the 82nd minute for Jones to score. He headed the ball into the net to equalize. Jones had been loaned to Bournemouth from Cardiff just 10 days earlier. After he scored, Jones celebrated with an acrobatic move, and his teammates crowded around him to celebrate earning a point from the game.

Australia’s coach, Darren Lehmann, supported his players after they were criticized for their behavior during Sunday’s World Cup final win against New Zealand. Wicketkeeper Brad Haddin was criticized for taunting New Zealand’s Martin Guptill after he was out. A photo of Haddin and James Faulkner making fun of Grant Elliott after he was dismissed also made the Australian team’s fifth World Cup victory controversial. Haddin clapped in Guptill’s face after the New Zealand batsman was bowled. However, Lehmann said Haddin was just following team instructions. He also pointed out that the International Cricket Council (ICC) did not punish the team, which showed they had not gone too far.

Rickie Fowler has won over more fans by defending his girlfriend, bikini model Alexis Randock, against an online bully. The bully, who goes by the name "fatalsplash," left a mean comment on a photo Alexis posted on Instagram. In the photo, Alexis and her sister Nicole are on the beach. The post was seen by Alexis’s 25,000 followers, including the bully, who called Alexis a "gold digger." Rickie Fowler spoke out to call out this unfair criticism.

Mark Wood tried on his new England cricket uniform this week. He liked it so much that he wore it around his house a lot. He was very happy to have it. Trying it on made him feel both nervous and excited.

Wood is 25 years old. He is 5 feet 11 inches tall and weighs just over 12 stone. This is not the usual size or shape for a fast bowler. He has been chosen for England’s team. The team will travel to the Caribbean on Thursday. They will play three Test matches against the West Indies. Wood has not played for England before, but he is part of the squad led by Alastair Cook.

England cricket player Ian Bell has agreed to stay with Warwickshire for three more years, meaning he will play for the club until the end of 2017. Bell first joined Warwickshire in 1999 after growing up in the club’s youth teams, starting with the Under-11 group. Now 32 years old, he has played 105 Test matches and 161 one-day international matches for England. With Warwickshire, Bell has won five trophies, including the County Championship in 2004 and 2012. Bell said, “As a true Warwickshire man, I am very happy to commit to this great club for another three years.”

Yorkshire has signed Indian cricketer Cheteshwar Pujara until the end of May. This happened after they ended the contract of Younus Khan. Younus was originally chosen as Yorkshire’s overseas player for 2015. However, he is now hoping to join Pakistan’s team for a possible tour of Bangladesh. This means he will not be able to play for Yorkshire in the LV= County Championship.

Instead, Pujara will join Yorkshire, who are the champions of Division One. This depends on him getting a work permit. Pujara played for Derbyshire at the end of last season, where he scored 219 runs in the championship.

Former Rangers striker Marco Negri says he left the club because he was afraid he had HIV. He joined Rangers from the Italian team Perugia in 1997 for £3.5 million. In his first 10 league games, he scored 23 goals. However, several injuries, including one during a reserve match against Aberdeen on November 13, 2000, hurt his career in Glasgow. Negri, a former forward for Rangers, revealed that he quit the team after fearing he had AIDS.

Raheem Sterling’s controversial campaign, which claimed that money wasn’t the main issue, took him to the Emirates Stadium. There, both Liverpool and Arsenal fans joined together to protest against the high cost of football for traveling supporters. One banner read, “£5bn and what do we get? £64 a ticket,” and was held by fans from both teams before the match started. Hopefully, Sterling understood the irony, even if it didn’t affect his performance on the field. It was a tough afternoon for him, as Arsenal won the game. Sterling struggled to make an impact, as he was surrounded by Arsenal players.

Former New Zealand rugby player Mils Muliaina was arrested for suspected sexual assault after his team, Connacht, played against Gloucester on Friday night. TV cameras showed police taking him away after the game.

Muliaina played 100 games for New Zealand before retiring after the 2011 World Cup. He joined Connacht at the start of this season and has played 11 games for them so far.

His team lost the match 14-7 at Kingsholm. Shortly after the game ended, he was led to a police van while the incident was shown live on television.

John Hartson recently looked back on his life as he turned 40. He shared that his serious health problems made him stop drinking heavily, quit gambling, and become a devoted husband. In 2009, when he was 33, doctors found that he had testicular cancer that had spread to his brain and lungs. Hartson wrote in the Scottish Sun that he felt like he was going to die when he got the news. The former soccer player for Celtic says this illness changed his life.

Leeds United owner Massimo Cellino says that Red Bull has made an offer to buy the club. Cellino, who is currently banned from working in the Football League, stated that Eleonora Sport, the company that owns most of Leeds, is looking at the offer. However, Leeds chairman Andrew Umbers said he did not know about any offer from Red Bull when he spoke to BBC Radio Leeds on Saturday morning. Cellino confirmed the bid to the Yorkshire Evening Post, saying, "There is an offer."

Steven Gerrard is leaving Liverpool at the end of the season after a long and successful career. In 1992, club legend Steve Heighway predicted in a newspaper article that Gerrard would be successful. Gerrard is now moving to the MLS team LA Galaxy for a new challenge. A newspaper from 1992 showed a photo of 12-year-old Gerrard, who was then a young talent in Liverpool’s academy. The article said, “Outstanding potential has to be recognised and nurtured and Stephen Gerrard, a gem from Huyton, could be the next on our production line.”

A Brazilian online football store says it is selling next season’s Chelsea jersey. The website shows three versions of the kit with the new "Yokohama" sponsor on the front, but without the Adidas logo. Most surprisingly, you can buy the shirt with "Bale 9" on the back. This is strange because Gareth Bale has had a difficult season at Real Madrid, and reports say he might return to England.

Darren Gough says he will always support Kevin Pietersen, no matter how difficult the playing conditions are. Gough, who is England’s ninth-best bowler ever, is a close friend of Pietersen and was the best man at his wedding. Pietersen has returned to play for Surrey in a final attempt to make England’s team for the Ashes cricket series this summer. Everyone is watching his upcoming match against Glamorgan in Cardiff, which starts in just over two weeks. Gough believes that Pietersen has only a small chance of being selected for the national team.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini admits that his team is now struggling to stay in the top four of the Champions League spots. They have fallen too far behind Chelsea in the race for the Premier League title. Their recent poor performance has made things worse, as other teams are catching up quickly. If results go against them this weekend, City could drop to fourth place before their next match against Crystal Palace on Monday. The text also notes that during Friday’s training session, Pellegrini shook hands with David Silva, while Martin Demichelis, Wilfried Bony, and Fernando were present.

David Villa seems happy with his move to Major League Soccer (MLS). As the captain of New York City FC, he is exploring his new home. The former Barcelona player has had a good start in the United States. He has scored one goal and helped his team reach third place in the Eastern Conference.

He posted a photo on Instagram showing his family visiting the Empire State Building. In the post, he wrote, "Beautiful Empire State Building!!"

New York City FC is currently two points behind their city rivals, the New York Red Bulls. Villa will want his team to beat them and win the bragging rights.

Kenny Dalglish says Harry Kane should not play for England’s Under-21 team this summer. Instead, Kane should save his energy for Roy Hodgson’s main national team.

Kane earned his first senior caps for England last week, but he is still allowed to play for Gareth Southgate’s young team. However, Dalglish believes Kane has shown he is ready for the big stage. He thinks Kane should stay fresh for the 2016 European Championships.

Kane scored his first goal for England shortly after coming off the bench. His performance against Italy showed that he can handle playing against some of the world’s best defenders.

Arsene Wenger says Arsenal must play perfectly until the end of the season if they want to win the title. However, he believes they will be ready if Chelsea makes a mistake.

Arsenal beat Liverpool 4-1 at home. Hector Bellerin, Mesut Ozil, Alexis Sanchez, and Olivier Giroud scored the goals. Arsenal is now seven points behind Chelsea, who are leading the Premier League. Chelsea will visit Arsenal in two weeks, but they still have one game left to play.

Wenger says his team must focus on winning every game so they are prepared if Chelsea loses points. He is keeping his team focused and not letting them get too excited about their recent win.

Consumers might soon have to pay a 10% sales tax, known as GST, on movies and music they download. The government wants to do this to earn extra billions of dollars. Treasurer Joe Hockey said that state governments have agreed to apply this tax to digital content from streaming services like Netflix and Apple. This change could also affect people who buy online items under $1,000 from other countries. This would impact big companies like Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and eBay.

No young person wants their parents to follow them on social media, and Deion Sanders Jr. found out why this week. He is a talented football player and a second-year student at Southern Methodist University. On Thursday, he posted a message on Twitter saying, "I get doughnuts from the neighborhood almost every morning. If they don’t come in a plain white box, I don’t want them!"

His father, Deion Sanders, saw the post and decided to tease his son. He replied, "You’re like a Huxtable with a million-dollar trust fund. Stop acting like you’re from the hood! Lololol. Son. #truth." The term "Huxtable" is sometimes used to describe wealthy Black people.

Wesley Sneijder has apologized for accidentally releasing his new knife collection in Galatasaray team colors on the 15th anniversary of a tragic event. On April 5, 2000, two Leeds United fans, Kevin Speight and Christopher Loftus, were stabbed to death in Istanbul’s Taksim Square before a soccer match against Galatasaray.

Sneijder made the mistake by posting on Twitter on the morning of a Championship game, announcing that his Galatasaray-themed knife set was now available for delivery. This happened just as Leeds and Blackburn Rovers were preparing to play, with a minute of silence scheduled before their match at Elland Road to honor the victims.

On Saturday afternoon, Arsenal beat Liverpool 4-1 at home in the Premier League. This win put them nine points ahead of Liverpool, who are their main rivals for a top-four spot.

Arsenal took an early lead with goals from Hector Bellerin, Mesut Ozil, and Alexis Sanchez, making the score 3-0. Jordan Henderson then scored a penalty for Liverpool to make it 3-1. Finally, Olivier Giroud scored a great goal in the extra time of the match to make the final score 4-1.

Sportsmail’s Matt Barlow now looks at how both teams played.

These close-up photos, taken by a student in Borneo, show how strong a weaver ant is. The tiny ant can tie a much larger and heavier centipede in knots. Even though the centipede is bigger, it cannot escape the ant’s grip. In the pictures, the centipede curls into a circle as it tries to get away.

For the first 10 minutes of the match between Arsenal and Liverpool at the Emirates Stadium, fans from both teams stayed in their seats to protest high ticket prices. They were angry about rising costs, especially after the Premier League announced a £5.14 billion deal for TV rights. Tickets for the game started at £64. The fans hoped that showing empty seats would highlight how hard it is for supporters to afford going to games.

Workers at US intelligence agencies, such as the CIA, NSA, and National Counterterrorism Center, watch graphic videos all day to find clues about where terrorists are and what they plan to do. These videos often show beheadings, violent attacks, and hardcore pornography, sometimes involving children. Because this work causes serious emotional stress, these agencies hire special psychologists and psychiatrists to help the workers cope with the trauma.

Men’s grooming company West Coast Shaving created a unique project where they combined the faces of members from famous rock bands into single images. The result is 30 blended faces representing 30 legendary bands.

In some of these images, specific band members are easy to recognize. For example, the picture of The Beatles looks like a blurry photo of a young Paul McCartney. Kurt Cobain’s features are clearly visible in the image for Nirvana, and Eddie Van Halen’s features stand out in the image for Van Halen.

Prosecutors are dropping nearly 30 criminal cases involving four Fort Lauderdale police officers. These officers were fired after an investigation found racist videos and text messages.

On Thursday, the Broward State Attorney’s Office said they had already dismissed 12 felony cases, 19 misdemeanor cases, and one case involving a juvenile. About 20 more dismissals are expected.

The cases include charges like burglary, possession of cocaine, and aggravated assault with a firearm. The officers who made the arrests are no longer working for the police department.

Jia Binhui, a 25-year-old man with leukemia, lies on hot coals every day in hopes of killing his cancer cells. He cannot afford hospital treatment, so he is trying this alternative method. According to People's Daily Online, experts told him that temperatures above 42 degrees Celsius can destroy cancer cells. Jia built a makeshift barbecue in his garden in Yunlong County, Yunnan Province, in southwest China. He lies on a grate above a fire, similar to how meat is cooked on a spit roast.

A takeaway shop owner in Gillingham has been fined nearly £15,000 for serious food safety violations. Inspectors found that pizza boxes at the business, called Pizza Plus Fried Chicken, were filled with mouse droppings and tomato puree that had gone moldy. The owner, Kunaratnam Kunanatha, 36, from Catford, London, admitted to seven offenses, including failing to clean properly, allowing a mouse infestation, and selling unsafe food. Inspectors also discovered that the food preparation areas were filthy.

Fenerbahce has asked for the Turkish soccer league to be paused after gunmen attacked their team bus on Saturday. The bus was shot at while driving to the airport after an away game against Caykur Rizespor. On their official website, Fenerbahce said the bus driver was hurt and taken to the hospital, but no one else was injured. There are marks on the bus’s windshield, and the window near the driver was broken. The driver, who had blood coming from a head wound, was seen asking for help after the attack.

Fran Kirby played very well for the England Women’s team, showing she deserves a spot in the World Cup starting lineup. She helped England beat China 2-1.

Kirby created the first goal for her teammate Jodie Taylor just one minute into the game. Later, Kirby scored the second goal herself. This was only her eighth game for the national team. Her goal made it 2-0, which made England look like they had won easily.

However, after the early success, England had trouble keeping their advantage. About 5,665 fans watched the match at Manchester City's Academy Stadium.

Wayne Rooney, the captain of Manchester United, scored a great goal in a 3-1 win against Aston Villa. This victory moved United up to third place in the Premier League, ahead of Manchester City.

The score was 1-0 after 79 minutes when Rooney made a smart move and kicked the ball with his right foot past the Aston Villa goalkeeper, Brad Guzan. This was his sixth goal in eight games for United. Manager Louis van Gaal had recently moved Rooney back to his usual forward position after he had been playing in midfield.

Wayne Rooney believes Manchester United is very likely to qualify for the Champions League, which makes this weekend’s game against Aston Villa very important. Under manager Louis van Gaal, United is currently fourth in the Premier League. They have a five-point lead over the teams trying to catch them. This advantage comes after they beat Liverpool 2-1, with Juan Mata scoring both goals. That win gave United a buffer over Liverpool, as well as over Southampton and Tottenham, who are also competing for a top-four spot. Rooney feels the team is on track to reach the Champions League.

Jose Mourinho, the manager of Chelsea football club, says he talks to God every day. However, he never talks about football with God, and he also never discusses the game with his wife, Matilde Faria.

Mourinho is a father of two. He says his family understands what it is like to be poor. He has been lucky enough to work with the World Food Programme as an ambassador to help fight hunger.

The 52-year-old manager tries hard to keep his work life separate from his family life. In an interview with the Daily Telegraph, he said he has strong faith in God. "I believe completely," he said. "I pray every day, and I speak with Him every day."

Jonathan Stevenson, who is now a director at LiveWire Sport, shared a letter from the late Australian cricket legend Richie Benaud on Twitter. Almost 20 years ago, when Stevenson was just 16 years old, he wrote to Benaud asking for advice on how to bowl left-handed leg spin. Benaud sent a detailed reply. Stevenson posted the letter on Friday as a tribute to Benaud, saying the response showed what a great man he was.

Richie Benaud, a famous Australian cricket commentator, has died at the age of 84. People are calling him a national treasure and a cricket legend. He had been receiving radiation treatment for skin cancer since November. On Thursday, he was admitted to a hospice in Sydney. He died peacefully in his sleep, with his wife, Daphne, and other family members by his side. Benaud played in 63 Test matches. He also helped create World Series Cricket in the 1970s and was one of the most well-known cricket commentators in the world. Many people are paying tribute to him as both a great commentator and one of Australia’s most important cricketers. Videos are available below.

Patrick O'Flynn, UKIP’s election campaign chief and economics spokesman, admitted that the party sometimes acts like a "rugby club on tour," with members who can be rude and sexist. He said UKIP needs to work harder because it is falling behind with female voters. O'Flynn made these comments while launching the party’s "policies for women" alongside deputy chairman Suzanne Evans and MEP Diane James. He had to defend the party’s "blokeish" image under Nigel Farage.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling’s agent, Aidy Ward. He suggested that Sterling is being influenced by outside forces and that he would likely stay at Liverpool if he made the decision on his own.

Rodgers made these comments after Liverpool lost 4-1 to Arsenal on Saturday, a loss that effectively ended their chances of qualifying for next season’s Champions League. His criticism came after a televised interview in which Sterling admitted he was flattered by Arsenal’s interest in him.

A 23-year-old man was arrested for the murder of Vanessa Santillan, a 33-year-old transgender escort from Mexico. Her body was found in a £400,000 flat in Fulham, southwest London, at the end of March. She died from injuries to her head and neck after being beaten and strangled. The suspect has been released on bail but must return to a London police station for further questioning at a later date.

Chelsea had to play very hard to win 3-0 against Stoke at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Eden Hazard was the best player for Jose Mourinho’s team. He scored the first goal calmly from a penalty kick. Then, Charlie Adam tied the game with an amazing shot from inside his own half, just before halftime. Stoke kept making things difficult for Chelsea until Asmir Begovic made a mistake, which let Loic Remy score the winning goal. Sportsmail’s Kieran Gill gave player ratings. For Chelsea, who played in a 4-2-3-1 formation: Thibaut Courtois got a score of 5.5. He did not have to make many saves in the first 43 minutes, but he was beaten by Adam’s incredible long-range shot

Derek Skyler Brux, a 22-year-old man from Wyoming, was sentenced to five years of probation and ordered to pay $63,000 in restitution to his employer, Rail Link. In January, Brux pleaded guilty to stealing two locomotives from a coal mine last fall. He was angry after a phone call with his boss, so he unhitched the trains and drove them at high speed for 13 miles along one of the busiest rail lines in the country. He then crashed into an inactive Union Pacific train at 10 mph, backed up, and hit it again.

Nearly 20 years ago, a young English cricket fan named Jonathon Stevenson wrote to Australian cricket legend Richie Benaud to ask for advice on how to bowl leg spin. Benaud sent a long, detailed reply.

On Friday, after Benaud died, Stevenson shared that letter on Twitter as a tribute. Stevenson, who is now a director at LiveWire Sport, said the reply showed what a great man Benaud was. Stevenson was only 16 years old when he first wrote to him.

Dan Klice, 57, was working as a judge at a track meet at Ramapo College in Mahwah, New Jersey. He lives in Oleans, New York, but traveled across the Hudson River to judge the event.

While watching the competition, Klice saw a javelin flying toward him. He tried to jump out of the way, but he tripped and fell. As he fell, his left heel was exposed, and the javelin hit him, sticking into his heel. Police say the javelin was off course when it hit him.

This season, the top of the Championship league has been very unpredictable, making it hard to guess who will win. However, Middlesbrough is currently in the best position.

With only four weeks left, Middlesbrough’s manager, Aitor Karanka, leads a division where the top spot has changed hands 15 times. There are eight teams within seven points of each other, with six matches still to play. But Middlesbrough knows that if they keep winning, no one can catch them.

They are one point ahead of second-place Bournemouth. Watford, who play Middlesbrough on Monday, are also one point behind, and Norwich is one point further back than that. The paragraph ends by noting that Middlesbrough’s Patrick Bamford

A young pig has become famous online because it learned to walk on its back legs. The pig was born without back legs, so it balances on its front legs. A video on People's Daily Online shows the pig taking shaky steps and keeping its nose close to the ground to find food. The video is popular because it is cute. The pig almost falls over several times, but it always manages to stay balanced.

Wigan Athletic quickly found a new manager to replace Malky Mackay. They chose Gary Caldwell, a former club captain, to help them avoid being relegated from the Championship.

Caldwell, who is 32 years old, has been with the team since 2010. He will manage his first game on Friday against Fulham at their stadium, Craven Cottage.

Many people were surprised by this choice. Even Caldwell said he did not expect to get the job. He has been given a long-term contract. Although he helped Wigan win the FA Cup in 2013, he now has to focus on keeping the team in the league.

A very young girl, likely between two and three years old and from China, has become famous online. In a video posted by People's Daily Online, she is seen dancing to music while balancing three small bowls on her head. She moves happily, bobbing and spinning slowly, and is careful not to drop the bowls. This video has gone viral in China, making her an internet sensation.

The fans were loud and clear, chanting, “Bees up, Fulham down.” This happened at Craven Cottage, in the section where Brentford’s 6,000 traveling supporters were watching. It was a day for them to enjoy their success. They showed again that they are strong contenders for a spot in the playoffs, making fun of their neighbors, Fulham, who used to be better than them. When Stuart Dallas scored his second goal of the day, the crowd booed Kit Symons, who went back to his coaching area. But the focus wasn’t on Fulham and their growing problems.

Peter Moores said he can work with Michael Vaughan if Vaughan becomes England’s new director of cricket, even though they have had problems in the past. Speaking in St Kitts on Thursday, Moores stated, “Of course I could.” He explained that it is not a personal issue and that people are allowed to have different opinions. He noted that the team is currently going through a change, and his main goal is to make England as strong as possible as quickly as possible. Moores said that whoever gets the job, he wants to share his ideas to ensure the best path forward. Although the new director is expected to be a powerful leader who works closely with the team, Moores was unsure if England needed another person giving orders in the dressing room.

Michael Vaughan, Alec Stewart, and Andrew Strauss are three former England captains who want to lead the team’s changes after Paul Downton was fired as managing director. All three had great success playing for England and are highly respected in the sport. Sportsmail looks at these three men, who are competing to become the most powerful person in English cricket.

Alec Stewart (52)
Current Job: Director of cricket at Surrey.
Achievements: He played 133 Test matches, which is more than any other England cricketer.
Players He Likes: He has built a good relationship with Kevin Pietersen, who was out of favor at Surrey. Stewart says English cricket needs to be bold.

Diego Costa will likely miss at least two weeks because he hurt his hamstring again. This happened during Chelsea’s 2-1 victory over Stoke City. As a result, he will probably miss upcoming Premier League games against Queens Park Rangers and Manchester United.

Jose Mourinho put Costa into the game at halftime because the score was tied 1-1. Charlie Adam had just scored a long goal to tie the match, after Eden Hazard had scored first. Shortly after coming on, Costa limped off the field with the injury. He looked sad as he sat on the ground after hurting his hamstring again.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers said that Mario Balotelli will not be playing for the team this summer. Balotelli decided not to travel to the game against Arsenal because he hurt himself slightly during practice on Friday.

Even if he had been healthy, Balotelli would not have started the match. He would have been a substitute, and he would have been lower on the list of available players than Daniel Sturridge, who was also on the bench. The £16 million striker was left out of the squad for the Arsenal game because of this minor training injury.

After Northampton lost badly to Clermont with a score of 37-5 in the Champions Cup, Tom Wood joked and thanked Clermont for letting Northampton train openly. Northampton, who are currently leading the English league by 10 points, were knocked out of the European competition in the quarter-finals. They lost because Clermont scored four tries to Northampton’s one. The game was effectively over by halftime, as Clermont had built an unbeatable 27-0 lead using strong forwards and skilled backs. After the match, Northampton players Calum Clark and Tom Wood, along with captain Dylan Hartley, walked off the field following the heavy defeat.

Robert Lewandowski scored the winning goal for Bayern Munich in a close victory against his former team, Borussia Dortmund, at Signal Iduna Park on Saturday. The Polish player, who left Dortmund last summer without a transfer fee, scored on his first return to the club. His goal helped Bayern Munich increase their lead at the top of the Bundesliga to 10 points. Lewandowski played for Dortmund for four years, helping them win two consecutive league titles. When he scored to put Bayern ahead just before halftime, he celebrated quietly. For more details, see Nicholas Godden’s full match report.

Sarazen, Hogan, Player, Nicklaus, Woods, and McIlroy. The biggest compliment to the man who might join these golf legends this week is that his name fits right in with them. Rory McIlroy could become only the sixth person to win the Grand Slam at Augusta National on Sunday. While this is the highest achievement in golf, he wants to do more than just fill his trophy case; he wants to be the main leader of his sport. Paul McGinley, Europe’s famous Ryder Cup captain, agrees. He explains McIlroy’s attitude simply: McIlroy is not like Jose Mourinho.

The fast greens at Augusta National can be scary for many people playing in the Masters for the first time. But Danny Willett from Sheffield was not worried. The 27-year-old finished with a score of 71, which is one stroke under par. He was especially happy about a long putt for an eagle on the 13th hole, and he posted about it on Twitter.

His brother, PJ Willett, was at home fixing light switches when he also tweeted: “Bro @willett1987 shot under par in the first round of his #Masters2015 debut. I swapped some switches. Who’s living the dream?”

Alan Stubbs says he was worried about crowd trouble if his team, Hibs, had formed a guard of honor for Hearts before their match in Edinburgh. Hearts’ head coach, Robbie Neilson, and defender Alim Ozturk criticized Hibs for not showing public respect to the league champions. Just over a week earlier, Rangers, Queen of the South, and Alloa had all lined up to applaud Hearts. Stubbs admitted that he did not ask the police for advice, but he insisted that the fear of unrest, not a lack of respect, was the reason for the decision.

Sam Allardyce is already planning for next season with West Ham, but he doesn’t know if he will still be the manager. His contract ends at the end of this season, and it is unclear what will happen with the club’s co-owners, David Gold and David Sullivan. West Ham has already scored two more points than they did last season, with seven games left to play. However, because the team has played poorly in 2015, there are rumors that Allardyce might be fired.

Thomas Bjorn had a tricky situation on the second hole, which is a par-five. His first shot went into the trees, so he hit the ball back onto the fairway for his third shot, leaving a 145-yard approach to the green. However, his aim was off. The ball hooked to the left, flew into the crowd, and landed in the lap of a female spectator during the first round of the Masters. Fortunately, Bjorn was allowed to take a free drop and continue playing the hole. He stayed calm, made a par, and played well.

A two-year-old boy named Blaine Taylor from Aberdeen, Scotland, cried after accidentally breaking his Easter egg. He was competing in a rolling race against his older brother, Cody. As Blaine tried to roll his egg down a grassy hill, he stepped on it, crushing the shell and yolk. Blaine said, "It's broken," and then started crying loudly. His father, Luke, filmed the accident and posted the video online. The video has been viewed more than 90,000 times.

At 85 years old, Arnold Palmer ignored his age and a shoulder injury to hit the ceremonial opening drive at the 79th Masters. This event provided the first major story of the year at Augusta National.

Palmer, a seven-time major champion, had been recovering from a dislocated shoulder, which kept him from participating in the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday. Despite the pain, he took his place on Thursday morning alongside Jack Nicklaus and Gary Player as the honorary starters. It did not matter that his shot hooked slightly toward the ninth fairway.

Natasha Jonas, a 30-year-old boxer from Liverpool, has announced that she is retiring from boxing. She was the first woman to box for Great Britain in the Olympics. At the 2012 London Games, she made history by fighting Katie Taylor from Ireland, who won the gold medal, in the first round of the women’s lightweight competition. Jonas has previously won bronze medals in world and European championships. She said it felt like the right time to stop. After taking time off to recover from a recent injury, she decided she did not want to return to the hard work of full-time training.

Two hours before the Miami Open semifinal, Novak Djokovic practiced his returns in an empty stadium. His hitting partner stood three feet inside the baseline to mimic John Isner’s powerful serve, sending the ball at Djokovic very quickly. This practice helped Djokovic break Isner’s serve during the match. He won on Friday night with a score of 7-6 (3), 6-2. Djokovic said, “He’s probably the best server we have in the game. But I managed to get a lot of serves back. That was one of the keys in the match, making him play and getting into the rally and making him work extra.” By beating John Isner in straight sets, Djokovic reached the final of the Miami Open.

Mauricio Pochettino, now 43, used to have long hair. In the 2002 World Cup, he was playing for Argentina when he tripped Michael Owen, which led to a penalty that David Beckham scored. Pochettino has since cut his hair to look more like a manager.

He has been in England for just over two years and has built a strong reputation. People admire not only his coaching skills but also his willingness to give young English players a chance. Recent research shows that young English players want to play for him. Because he trusts homegrown talent, Pochettino might be the key to saving English football.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton have had disagreements in the past year, but they agreed on what to do on Thursday. After losing to Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel at the Malaysian Grand Prix on March 29, the two Mercedes teammates worked with their team to stop Ferrari from winning the next race in China. They visited the Mercedes factory in Brackley to find a way to win the race in Shanghai, which takes place from April 10 to 12.

Formula One legend Jackie Stewart is worried about the decline of the German Grand Prix. He is urging F1 leaders not to sacrifice tradition for money, especially as there are fewer races in Europe. The German Grand Prix was removed from the 2015 schedule because of financial issues. Meanwhile, Bernie Ecclestone, who handles F1’s business, could not promise that the famous Italian Grand Prix would continue. The Italian race was uncertain because it was unclear which track would host it, as Hockenheim and Nurburgring had been sharing the role in recent years. Additionally, F1 races are moving away from Europe to more profitable locations in the Middle East.

Lewis Hamilton has driven very well for Mercedes over the past year, but he recently admitted to making a mistake off the track. At 30 years old, his success has allowed him to meet famous people from sports, entertainment, and politics. Seven years ago, at Nelson Mandela’s 90th birthday party, Hamilton accidentally stepped on former U.S. President Bill Clinton’s foot. He shared this story on the Clare Balding Show, noting that the incident happened in 2008.

Repair work has begun on the roof of the Silverstone motor racing circuit, which was damaged by strong winds over the weekend. The high winds on Sunday and Monday affected part of the "Wing," a three-story corporate building worth $40 million (£27 million) that hosts Formula One’s British Grand Prix. Social media images showed that a section of the roof had been blown off. Despite this damage, Silverstone’s sporting director, Stuart Pringle, says that upcoming events will not be affected.

Lewis Hamilton, a two-time Formula One world champion, talked about what his tattoos mean in an interview with Men's Health magazine. He is the leader of the drivers' championship after the first two races of the 2015 season, having finished first and second. The 30-year-old driver, who races for Mercedes, is on the cover of the May issue of the magazine. In the interview, which was released on Thursday, April 2, he explained the significance of his body art.

Jason Robinson, who won the World Cup with England, has said that he once thought about killing himself. This happened during a difficult time in his career when he was arrested for violent crimes.

He spoke about this in a documentary called *Jason Robinson: Sports Life Stories*, which will air on ITV4 on Tuesday at 10 pm. The 40-year-old former rugby player admitted that he drank heavily when he first started playing for the Wigan rugby league club. This drinking habit almost ruined his career.

Robinson, who scored a try for England in the 2003 World Cup final win against Australia, said, "I got into a situation where I was drinking sometimes six nights a week."

Zimbabwe might become the first Test-playing nation to visit Pakistan since gunmen attacked the Sri Lankan team bus in Lahore six years ago. Shaharyar Khan, who leads the Pakistan Cricket Board, says Zimbabwe is ready to play five one-day matches in Pakistan. He hopes the tour will happen next month.

Khan will meet with officials from the Zimbabwe Cricket Union next week in Dubai during an ICC meeting. He said, "I hope you will receive good news very soon." Elton Chigumbura, Zimbabwe’s captain for limited-overs cricket, could lead his team in Pakistan. The Pakistan Cricket Board chairman hopes to start the five-match series as soon as May.

Tim Sherwood says he is still in contact with Tottenham Hotspur chairman Daniel Levy. He even thanks the club’s board for letting him go, because that decision allowed him to become the manager of Aston Villa.

Levy fired Sherwood as Tottenham’s head coach at the end of last season. He replaced him with Mauricio Pochettino. This ended Sherwood’s five months as head coach and his six years working with the club’s youth teams.

Instead of being angry about leaving, Sherwood spoke highly of Levy, who has been with the club since 2001, and his former employers. Sherwood will manage Aston Villa when they play Tottenham in London on Saturday.

Alex Rodriguez came back to play for the New York Yankees on the first day of the baseball season. He had been suspended for 162 games, which covered the entire 2014 season, because he admitted to using performance-enhancing drugs from a clinic in Florida. He played as the designated hitter and batted seventh. Despite his suspension, fans welcomed him warmly, with some holding up signs that said "Forgive." His teammates also applauded him as he went onto the field.

The new county cricket season is starting soon. The first matches of the Championship will begin this Sunday across the country. Yorkshire wants to keep their Division One title. Kevin Pietersen hopes his batting will help Surrey move up from the second tier. Mark Butcher, a former player for Surrey and England, gives his advice on the County Championship.
